The communication sub-system is crucial for these nanosatellites, and the antenna is the core element. To push the forefront, the challenging field of CubeSat antennas design demands for innovative design methodologies, new materials and disruptive manufacturing approaches, such as additive manufacturing. Considering specific mission requirements, combined with the harsh space environment, a given antenna layout must effectively perform. To this aim, multiphysics simulations can help in discriminating between different design, while favoring the understanding of potential risky situations. This work deals with the presentation of methodologies for designing innovative antennas for CubeSat applications. In particular, a 3D-printed curved stacked patch antenna working in the S-band and a stacked patch antenna array working in the Ka-band will be presented. The electromagnetic performances of the antennas have been studied with a numerical multiphysics model considering the thermal and mechanical variations during a simulated CubeSat mission.

articleTitle: Women in Electrical Engineering – Serbian Story: Mission Ongoing!
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Women’s impacts in science and engineering have reached far beyond what women had ever imagined. The Serbian story: Mission ongoing is about Serbian IEEE Women in Engineering Affinity Group activities. It celebrates some of many Serbian women that had not only designed innovative solutions but also inspired young women to pursue engineering careers and introduces promising young female engineers.

articleTitle: A Formal Account for Reasoning About Uncertain Probabilities in Intelligence Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In the sixth assessment of the international panel on climate change (IPCC) one can read sentences such as “cumulative net CO2 emissions over the last decade (2010-2019) are about the same size as the 11 remaining carbon budget likely to limit warming to 1.5C (medium confidence).” Such reports are very common in the intelligence community, but a formal account for dealing with the degree of belief and of confidence is still missing. In this paper, we propose a formal account for allowing such degrees of belief and the associated confidence to be used to label arguments in abstract argumentation settings. We focus on the task of probabilistic inference over a chosen query building upon Sato’s distribution semantics which has been already shown to encompass a variety of cases including the semantics of Bayesian networks. Borrowing from the vast literature on such semantics, we examine how such tasks can be dealt with in practice when considering uncertain probabilities.

articleTitle: Organizing Structures and Information for Developing AI-enabled Military Decision-Making Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Background: AI-enabled decision-making systems play a critical role in the planning and execution of effect-based approach operations (following an effect-based approach), thereby empowering armed forces. The crucial aspect is to figure out what kind of AI-enabled system we can or should build to be successful, taking into account the current and future technologies available. Aims: This paper aims to eliminate ambiguity surrounding military decision-making systems by replacing the term “AI-enabled“ with the more accurate and realistic “AI-automated.“ It is important to note that the current focus of researchers and the government is on building AI applications that can assist commanders and staff in streamlining the decision-making process, rather than creating systems that can make decisions. The primary objective is to identify the AI technology required to improve future C2 systems and then act accordingly. An important point is that computer-assisted processes already provide efficiency. Therefore, the appropriate question to address is: “Should AI be used to enhance the automation of the decisionmaking process, or should AI itself be used to drive the decision-making process?“ Methods: The study suggests that experimentation should guide the understanding of appropriate AI-enabled technology for C2 system development. The following discusses the necessary approach to follow. Results: Although conducting experiments on this topic is challenging and costly due to the lack of AI-enabled systems, previous studies have conducted some of the feasible experiments that validate our initial interpretation. These findings highlight the importance of further research in the suggested direction and indicate the need for a deeper understanding of the topic. Conclusions: Meanwhile, a possible method for the armed forces to be ready for upcoming AI technologies involves creating an organization, the Military Experience Factory, which is committed to gathering high-quality data from military units carrying out operations.

articleTitle: Detecting Targeted Phishing Websites for Brand Protection and Cyber Defence Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Cybercrime continues to pose a significant threat to modern society, requiring a solid emphasis on cyber-attack prevention, detection and response by civilian and military organisations aimed at brand protection. This study applies a novel framework to identify, detect and mitigate phishing attacks, leveraging the power of computer vision technology and artificial intelligence. The primary objective is to automate the classification process, reducing the dwell time between detection and executing courses of action to respond to phishing attacks. When applied to a real-world curated dataset, the proposed classifier achieved relevant results with an F1-Score of 95.76% and an MCC value of 91.57%. These metrics highlight the classifier’s effectiveness in identifying phishing domains with minimal false classifications, affirming its suitability for the intended purpose. Future enhancements include considering a fuzzy logic model that accounts for the classification probability in conjunction with the domain creation date and the uniqueness of downloaded resources when accessing the website or domain.

articleTitle: A Novel, Multimodal, High Throughput Screening Microscope Platform for Automating the Analysis a of Vast Populations of Forensics Traces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: We have developed a novel, multimodal microscope platform, capable of acquiring hyperspectral, fluorescence and polarimetry imaging modes. This multidimensional data structure is processed by an integrated machine learning platform, which creates trace identification maps for a plurality of millimeter scale fields. The system can accommodate a vast population of traces in fully automated, ultrafast and unsupervised manner.

articleTitle: A Consensus-Based Kalman Filter for Target Localization in Emergency Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In the last years, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have been widely used for several types of missions, including aerial reconnaissance, search and rescue, and military operations. In first rescue missions, the ability to detect missing people after avalanche events in a short time is fundamental to increase the probability of saving them. The use of unmanned aerial vehicles in such scenarios can improve results with respect to multiple points of view: on the one hand, it can decrease the danger for rescuers, while on the other hand, it can speed up the search process. An effective solution can be the involvement of a formation of multiple drones to cover a greater research space and accelerate the process. However, an important challenge in deploying a formation of robots in emergency scenarios is the autonomy in terms of system scalability, since drones are usually teleoperated in a one-to-one ratio with operators, requiring a large crew of rescuers. In order to improve the situational awareness and distribute the communication burden, this paper deals with a decentralized Kalman filtering algorithm using sensor data from multiple drones to estimate a target position, besides UAVs state to support guidance and control algorithms. Such decentralized Kalman filtering algorithm combines the characteristics of Consensus on Information and Consensus on Measurement techniques. The proposed technique is preliminarily validated by means of numerical simulations on an example scenario.

articleTitle: Optimal Reconfiguration Planning for Large UAV Groups
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Today, the use of copter-type UAVs in various sectors is economically justified and sometimes has no alternative. The next step toward increasing the efficiency of this technology is to use groups of UAVs united by a single task. If such groups contain a large number of drones located quite densely, they are called swarms. A well-known example of the use of quadcopter swarms is the creation of visual images in the sky and their transformation according to a specific program. Obviously, the possibilities of such structures are much wider and they have very good prospects in the future. But to realize such opportunities, a number of tasks need to be solved, ranging from methods of obtaining and exchanging current information between group members to strategic planning and operational management of individual devices. These tasks are burdened by additional security conditions for optimal functioning. In this article, we consider the problem of geometric reconfiguration of a large group of UAVs from the actual initial state to the desired final state. For each vehicle, it is necessary to determine the endpoint to which it will move. Such a problem has more than one solution, so the optimality criterion was added as minimization of the complete reconfiguration duration. The problem is considered under the conditions of the same and constant flight speed of a copter type UAV. It is impossible to analyze all possible options, since the computational complexity of this method is proportional to N factorial, where N is the number of UAVs in the group. A quasi-optimal method has been developed, the complexity of which is proportional to N. By statistical modeling, its effectiveness has been proved, which can be compared with the effectiveness of the optimal method. Indirect estimates of its efficiency in the general case are also obtained. Specific examples of swarm reconfiguration are considered. The centralized structure of the UAV swarm is described, which should ensure optimal planning of the reconfiguration of a group of UAVs in practice.

articleTitle: Proactive and Predictive Risk Management in Aviation Safety: a corporate strategic approach.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper discusses the three worldwide approaches currently used for aviation risk management: reactive, proactive and predictive.Whilst reactive and proactive approaches make use of past occurrences and try respectively to solve issues and mitigate risks, the predictive approach looks further beyond the line of sight, to identify hazards and risks that have not been recognized or materialized, yet.The need to predict future safety risks is rather valuable for commercial aviation, but it has become paramount in military aviation due to the increasingly demanding and complex operational scenarios.Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning could play an important role in achieving fully predictive Aviation Safety. However, this will require engineering and subject matter expert resources which are often unaffordable in parallel to normal operations.Nevertheless, reactive and proactive risk management are consolidated practices which have shown their strength and have a margin for improvement. In this context, predictive risk management will undoubtedly bring advantages to the safety management of any organization, but it requires an important sustained effort, especially in the engineering field.Therefore, the leadership shall define its level of ambition by allocating appropriate resources to developing predictive risk management, while keeping the focus on proactive safety, which still provides its revenues.

articleTitle: Boosting the automated Information Processing for Reconnaissance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The emerging complexities due to an increasing availability of data sources and advanced technologies for data and information processing in the defense sector require careful considerations. In this study, we looked at the different aspects related to the exploitation of the advancing technologies for the reconnaissance operations. Specifically, system architecture, data fusion, human in the loop and knowledge modeling are explored, with an exemplary case of Large Language Models (LLM) on reconnaissance data is shown.

articleTitle: IoT, ML for Combat Identification: Technologies to reduce Blue on Blue events in Military Battlefield
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The NATO initiative on Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) is a long-term effort to connect military assets across space, air, land, sea, and cyber domains. The Department of Defense (DOD) intends for JADC2 to analyze warfighting data across all of those domains to allow decision makers to identify, execute, and monitor operations more effectively.A fundamental component of this awareness is the Combat Identification (CID) System, i.e the ability to identify in real-time the position and the status (friendly, unknown, foe) of units, in high-intensity, fast-paced battle scenarios, in order to reduce Blue on Blue (or friendly-fire) events and save life. In this paper we review how Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (ML) impact both on current and future Blue Force Tracking (BFT) decision support systems and CID implementation.

articleTitle: Active Thermography for Gunshot Residue (GSR) Pattern Estimation on Textiles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Gunshot residue (GSR) analysis on textiles plays a crucial role in forensic investigations. These residues vary in size and shape depending on the shooting distance; this relationship is evaluated by testing a new methodology of textile observation using active thermography. By integrating active infrared (IR) thermography with image processing techniques, the contrast between gunpowder particles and the cloth background is enhanced, facilitating reliable detection and analysis. The observed infrared emission patterns provide insights into the behavior and the distribution of gunpowder dispersion, aiding in determining the shooting distance. The analysis of GSR dispersion on the cloth reveals the presence of an increasing trend in the relationship between the shooting distance and the distance from which gunshot residue was detected, demonstrating the effectiveness of active thermography in detecting gunshot residue patterns up to a firing distance of about 30 cm. Beyond this distance, the signal-to-noise ratio decreases significantly, presenting problems in accurately identifying the presence of residues. The advantages of active thermography are underlined, including its non-intrusive and non-destructive nature and the elimination of the necessity for chemical reagents, simplifying the analysis process as potential tool for determining shooting distance.

articleTitle: ChatGPT Act as an Intelligence Officer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically ChatGPT, to facilitate the work of intelligence officers. LLMs have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language processing and generation, making them valuable tools for information retrieval, analysis, and decision-making. This paper presents an initial overview of the capabilities of LLMs in intelligence operations. Through a case study on ChatGPT, we illustrate how intelligence officers can leverage LLMs to enhance their work, including data collection, fusion, analysis, report generation, and information sharing. The results showcase the vast potential and the limits of LLMs in supporting intelligence officers in their complex and demanding tasks.

articleTitle: Digital Security by Design: A Review of Combined Hardware-Software-Based CyberSecurity with Compartmentalization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Compartmentalization serves as a cornerstone for fortified hardware and software security. This technique encompasses memory isolation, trusted execution environments, and hardware-based security mechanisms. Software compartmentalization includes sandboxing, virtualization, microservices, and code isolation, collectively mitigating security breaches and vulnerabilities while enhancing resilience. Uniquely, this paper introduces the innovative fusion of the Morello board, distinguished for fine-grained compartmentalization, with CheriBSD. Positioned within the convergence of Operational Technology (OT) and Information Technology (IT), Morello bridges Real-Time Digital Simulators (RTDS) and Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs)/sensors. By orchestrating previously unexplored territory, this work underscores the novel potential of Morello and CheriBSD in fortifying security for OT/IT integration, yielding unprecedented outcomes in the realm of cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Exploring Essential Wireless Technologies for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In order autonomous vehicles to be driven as independently as possible from human intervention, they will need a huge amount of data delivered from many different information sources dynamically and asynchronously while in motion. It is necessary to select technologies for wireless connection between them and information transport infrastructure that provide the most timely, accurate and secure data. Nowadays there a numerous of choices and this article will describe their important characteristics in competitive manner by predefined criteria.

articleTitle: Digital Chain of Custody Operational Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Managing digital evidence is intricate due to the growing intricacies of digital data. It holds a crucial role in legal proceedings, but ensuring the credibility of digital evidence and upholding the chain of custody’s integrity is challenging. Conventional evidentiary standards inadequately audit digital evidence metadata, creating discrepancies between traditional and digital custody.Digital evidence presents unique features that further complicate its administration. These include the ease of duplication, transfer, alteration, and deletion of digital data, making it susceptible to contamination. Moreover, digital evidence can seamlessly cross borders and is often time-sensitive. Existing standards exhibit gaps in the digital chain of custody, causing inconsistencies among stakeholders and EU member states. Standardizing the digital chain of custody (dCoC) is vital for evidence consistency and court admissibility.This paper proposes a standardized dCoC process that safeguards digital evidence’s integrity, enhances transparency, and fosters accountability. It introduces novel concepts like digital custody metadata (DCM), specifying transfer purposes and prompting custodianship at Custody Transfer Points (CTPs). A case study demonstrates the concept’s application, developed within the STRATEGY project and submitted to the CEN/TC 391 standardization body. It offers a new European standard for consistent and reliable digital evidence management.

articleTitle: Meta-Covers for Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In this contribution, we discuss the design of meta-covers coating antenna systems in view of defense and security applications. We review some of our recent results in the development of functionalized metasurface-based devices covering wire antennas for achieving unprecedented system functionalities such as cloaking, frequency reconfigurability and radiation pattern manipulation. These realistic applications are assets by exploring the broad potential of conformal metasurfaces made either uniform, non-uniform, non-linear or time-variant and represent a collection of some of the most relevant results where the reconfigurability of the antenna system is shifted at the physical layer.
